chunks: Aban, from Al-Fazeyl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Uthman said to Al-Miqdad, 'By Allah, you will cease [insulting me] or I will return you to your First Lord.' He said: 'So when death presented itself to Al-Miqdad, he said to Ammar, 'Convey to Uthman from me that I have returned to my First Lord.'

key_terms.رَبِّكَ الْأَوَّلِ: Your First Lord (God), a phrase used here to emphasize ultimate divine accountability
key_terms.عُثْمَانُ: Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rashidun Caliph
key_terms.لِلْمِقْدَادِ: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, a companion of the Prophet known for his outspokenness

ai.seo_question: What is the story behind Uthman's phrase 'I will return you to your First Lord'?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the dynamic between political authority and scholarly integrity, where Al-Miqdad’s witty retort to Uthman underscores the concept of ultimate accountability to God rather than temporal rulers. In Shia tradition, this exchange is often cited to validate the right of the *Fuqaha* to critique caliphal decisions, emphasizing that their primary allegiance is to divine truth. The narrative serves as a paradigm for the scholar's role in maintaining religious independence amidst political pressure.
